about: The expert council, item 5 (queue expert-council): the 15-minute monthly close. A finance chief closes the books every month so that no surprise is older than thirty days, and reports a few numbers, the reason for the biggest change and one decision. Here it is for a household. Paraphrased from common practice; content only, the screen is not built yet. Thresholds are planning rules of thumb, not advice; the person can change each one.

loop.cue: The first weekend after the salary or main income arrives (calendar item proposed: council-monthly-close, monthly, 15 minutes).
loop.smallestStep: The floor: read the three numbers the app already has and tap Closed. Two minutes.
loop.reward: The month is stamped Closed; a row of closed months grows; net worth change shows as one calm number.
loop.environment: Numbers arrive by themselves where they can (shared bank and fund messages); the close only asks about what is missing.
loop.review: Every third close ends with one extra question: is the close itself still 15 minutes? Drop a step that never changed a decision.
loop.constraint: Missing numbers. If a balance is older than 40 days the close asks for that one first and nothing else.

steps.ask: What is in the bank accounts today?
steps.source: changes: shared bank messages, else one number per account

steps.ask: What came in, and what went out?
steps.source: derived from the month's messages; the person corrects, never types the list

steps.ask: Which one category moved most against its usual level, and was it a one-off?
steps.source: derived: this month against the average of the last three

steps.ask: Is anything owed or due in the next 30 days (card bill, premium, fee, tax, EMI change)?
Investments and loans: any balance older than 40 days?
steps.source: changes: statements shared in, else one number each

steps.ask: What is the one decision this month?
steps.source: the app proposes one from the signals below

signals.name: Saving rate
signals.how: what was saved and invested, divided by take-home
signals.watch: below the person's own target for two months running
signals.decision: Raise the automatic transfer on salary day by a small step, or name the one cost to cut.

signals.name: Months of runway
signals.how: cash and liquid funds divided by essential monthly cost
signals.watch: under 6 months (under 12 for a business owner or a single earner)
signals.decision: Send this month's surplus to the emergency fund before anything else.

signals.name: Net worth change
signals.how: assets minus loans, against last month and a year ago
signals.watch: down for three months for reasons other than markets
signals.decision: Find the leak: a loan growing, or spending from savings.

signals.name: Fixed costs share
signals.how: rent or EMIs, fees, insurance and utilities, divided by take-home
signals.decision: One fixed cost to renegotiate, refinance or end this quarter.

signals.name: Loan payments share
signals.decision: No new loan; prepay the costliest one first.

decisionRule: Exactly one decision per close, the first signal on watch in the order above; if none is on watch, the decision is: keep going, and move the surplus to the next goal.

yearEnd.text: January to March: check tax-saving investments and the regime choice against the year's real income.
yearEnd.confirm: The income-tax department's calculator or your tax adviser

yearEnd.text: Once a year: is life and health cover still right for the income, loans and family as they are now?
Once a year: bring investments back to the planned split.
Once a year: list every subscription and standing instruction; end what was not used in 90 days.

persona.who: Salaried couple with a home loan

persona.note: Use the average of the last six months as take-home.
Saving rate is replaced by: spending against the planned yearly draw.
